note: Hand-curated (2026-08-13). amt = $ thousands per year. Priorities spend from the budget; revenue policies add to it. Sources per item; keep amounts defensible and cite where each number comes from.

priorities.name: Universal free school meals
priorities.who: Free breakfast and lunch for every public-school student — the state picks up all meal co-payments at expected participation. Act 139 (2025) already covers families under 300% of the poverty line; this finishes the job.
priorities.src: Hawaiʻi Appleseed UFSM analysis / DOE School Food Services Branch FY2025 ($32.6M at projected participation)

priorities.name: Create a state child tax credit
priorities.who: A $650 refundable credit per keiki aged 0–18. Twelve states already have one; the 2021 federal expansion cut child poverty nearly in half while it lasted.
priorities.src: Hawaiʻi Appleseed proposal ($650/child); cost modeled as $650 × ~284,000 keiki (ACS under-18), before any income cap

revenue.name: Raise the GET by half a point
revenue.who: 4% → 4.5% on nearly every transaction. The biggest single lever the state has — but the GET raises the cost of living and hits low-income families hardest.
revenue.src: Computed: FY2027 projected general-fund GET $4.69B ÷ 8 (half of the 4% rate)

revenue.name: Modernize the conveyance tax
revenue.who: Rates haven't moved since 2009. Marginal rates cut the tax for most residents while raising it on high-value investment property and out-of-state buyers (HB 2049-style).
revenue.src: Hawaiʻi Budget Primer FY2026-27 tax-fairness section: $70–80M/yr (midpoint used)

revenue.name: Tax investment profits like paychecks
revenue.who: Capital gains are taxed at 7.25% while wages pay up to 13%. Taxing them as ordinary income raises $85–132M a year — 88% of it from the top 1%.
revenue.src: Hawaiʻi Budget Primer FY2026-27 / ITEP: $85–132M/yr (midpoint used)

revenue.name: Close corporate loopholes
revenue.who: Worldwide combined reporting stops multinationals from shifting the profits they earn in Hawaiʻi offshore — the same standard small local businesses already meet.
